newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London market breezes through 4,000 level.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London market breezes through 4,000 level.

text.p: The psychologically important 4,000-level on the key FTSE index point proved little barrier to the London stock market on Wednesday as shares pushed ahead to another all-time high.
The initial surge in stocks took the FTSE 100 of leading shares to a new record of 4,014.4 shortly after the opening, topping its previous best of 3,994.1 set September 20.
Buying pressure quickly slackened off, however, leaving the market tracking sideways by late morning at 4,004.8, a rise of 12.6 points on the session.

An influx of cash from institutional investors at the start of the fourth quarter on Tuesday and robust performances in bond markets, encouraged by signs of moderate growth and benign inflationary pressures in Britain and America, have created a solid backcloth for the market's rise.
A large trading programme started late on Tuesday and weighted to the buy side, added the final piece to the jigsaw.
Recent rises have been underpinned by hopes of more money coming into the market while the rise has forced institutions with large cash holdings to invest so as not to miss out on further gains.

Fund management group PDFM, with around 15 percent of its holdings in cash is an extreme example, but many other institutions also hold sizeable amounts of cash and hopes this may go into shares continues to underpin sentiment.
"In the very short term, it does appear there's quite a lot of cash sitting on the sidelines waiting to come in," said Panmure Gordon strategist Ian Williams.

"On a week to two week view there's probably more upside to come... over the fourth quarter as a whole we're still a little bit nervous but the underlying liquidity driver is going to be the factor in the near future."

Overnight comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that there were no threats to inflation down the track added to the upbeat mood in London markets and raised hopes interest rates may not need to rise in the near future.

But unease at the current levels of London and New York markets and worries that a reluctance to raise interest rates ahead of elections on both sides of the Atlantic has left some warning of sharp corrections ahead.

"We remain cautious looking into next year both as a function of our concerns regarding the U.S. and more particulary with regard to UK monetary policy post the election. To a certain extent what's good today may be bad tommorrow for the markets," said Nomura's Nick Knight who has a 3,600 year-end target for the FTSE 100.
The wild card, according to Knight, is the United States and belated recognition towards the end of the year about the outlook for next year.
"I'm not particulary inclined to raise my target because it more reflects our concerns about next year," he added.
The market's charge to another record was mirrored on Wall Street overnight where the blue chip Dow Industrials index broke 5,900 for the first time and looks to have 6,000 firmly in its sights.
The Dow finished with a gain of nearly 23 points at a new record close of 5,904.9 and is expected to continue its run when trading begins in New York this afternoon.
The next big hurdle for markets is the closely watched U.S. payroll data due to be released on Friday which will provide further evidence of the state of the U.S. economy.
